name: LCK proto-oncogene, Src family tyrosine kinase

function.text: LCK encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Lck. Annotated molecular activities include protein tyrosine kinase activity and non-membrane spanning protein tyrosine kinase activity. It participates in intracellular signal transduction and hemopoiesis.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to severe combined immunodeficiency due to LCK deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal recessive; definitive GenCC assertion from ClinGen. Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: LCK encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Lck. It is a non-receptor tyrosine-protein kinase that plays an essential role in the selection and maturation of developing T-cells in the thymus and in the function of mature T-cells. It contributes to T-cell antigen receptor (TCR)-linked signal transduction pathways. It associates directly with the cytoplasmic tail of CD2, which leads to hyperphosphorylation and activation of LCK.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with severe combined immunodeficiency due to LCK deficiency (autosomal recessive).
